statement: The function returns a result r. Let vals(r)=[b_0,...,b_{m-1}]. Then m=2n-1; for every i with 0<=i<n, b_{2i}=a_i; and for every i with 0<=i<n-1, b_{2i+1}=gcd(a_i,a_{i+1}).
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n. Write gcd(x,y) for the greatest positive integer dividing both x and y.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the number of nodes in r is 2n-1, where n is the number of nodes in head.
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0<=i<n, the node at 0-based position 2i of r exists and has value a_i. Thus the original nodes occur in r in the same order and with unchanged values.
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0<=i<n-1, the node at 0-based position 2i+1 of r exists and has value gcd(a_i,a_{i+1}).
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n. Write gcd(x,y) for the greatest positive integer dividing both x and y.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0<=i<n-1, the node at 0-based position 2i+1 of r exists, and its value divides both a_i and a_{i+1}.
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0<=i<n-1, the node at 0-based position 2i+1 of r exists; writing v for its value, for every positive integer d, if d divides both a_i and a_{i+1}, then d divides v.
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every node value in r lies in the interval [1,1000].
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0<=i<n-1, the node at 0-based position 2i+1 of r exists; writing v for its value, 1 <= v <= a_i and 1 <= v <= a_{i+1} (equivalently, 1 <= v <= min(a_i,a_{i+1})).
preconditions: Let vals(L) be the sequence of values of the nodes of L from head to tail. The input head satisfies vals(head)=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}] with n>=1, n<=5000, and 1<=a_i<=1000 for every 0<=i<n.
